questions.question: How should I register this work on the board?

options.label: One epic + claim it (Recommended)
options.description: Create a single epic issue with the 4 capabilities as a checklist, claim it now, and start on the first piece (trigger). Sub-issues split off later as each piece firms up.

options.label: Epic + 4 sub-issues
options.description: Create the epic plus a separate issue per capability (trigger / inventory / stale / migrate) up front, then claim one to start.

options.label: Just one issue, don't claim yet
options.description: File the epic for tracking but hold off claiming/working it — you want to scope or prioritize against other tickets first.

questions.question: Where should I start the actual work once claimed?

options.label: Trigger new work
options.description: The genuinely new piece: a command to spawn a fresh session/task on Claude-cloud or Codex from a prompt + target repo.

options.label: Unified inventory
options.description: First build one cross-engine 'what's running where' view (extend `sessions` to also cover Codex), since trigger/migrate build on knowing current state.

options.label: Stale detection
options.description: First unify liveness + usage-limit into one 'stale work' report across both engines.

options.label: Design doc first
options.description: Write a short design/spec doc for the whole orchestration layer before coding any slice.

I'm in the `ai-harness` repo (worktree `bridge-cse_01C3q3aBYqrJqJeeTQdXieCA` on macmini), transcript is fresh. Here's what's open to pick up.

Since this worktree is in **ai-harness**, the directly-relevant tickets are the **Remote Control (#2)** ones:

- **#5** — Resume mechanism: decide 'true retry' vs injected continue; confirm anthropic_cloud parity
- **#6** — Codex approval rules: make force-push prompt again (normal push stays allowed)
- **#7** — Optional: report Claude.ai not GC-ing dead `env_*` entries from Remote Control dropdown
- **#12** — [AH] Verify Codex auto-resume end-to-end against a real usage-limit pause (item 3 of #3)

The other boards (FamilyFund #1, Job Search #3) have plenty too, but those live in other repos. Which would you like to claim?
Understood — go ahead and tell me which one you'd like (any board is fine, including the FamilyFund #1 or Job Search #3 items), or name an issue number directly and I'll check + claim it.

Actually, I want to register a different work, which is I wanna have scripts that are able to trigger new work on, um, both, uh, cloud code and codex and eventually create, um, also detect all the work that is currently being done, detect the ones that are stale, and have eventually an option of moving work from one to another.

Got it — you want to register a **new** ticket (not pick an existing one): a unified tooling layer to **trigger**, **inventory**, **stale-detect**, and eventually **migrate** work across both Claude Code (cloud) and Codex.

Before I draft the ticket, let me ground it in what already exists in the repo so it doesn't reinvent `agent_claims.sh` / `remote_control`. Quick look:

Lots of relevant scaffolding already — notably `session_port/` (claude↔codex), `session_fork.py`, `session_list.py`, `discovery.py`, and `usage_limit/`. Let me read the key ones so the ticket builds on them rather than duplicating.

Here's the gap analysis. Several of your four asks already have building blocks in `remote_control/`; the new work is mainly the **trigger** piece and a **unified cross-engine** layer over the rest:

| Capability | Today | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| **Trigger new work** (Claude cloud + Codex) | — `fork` clones an existing session; nothing starts fresh work from a prompt | **New**: spawn a new session/task on a chosen engine+repo from a prompt |
| **Inventory in-flight work** | `sessions` lists live Claude sessions w/ host (cloud/this-host/other-host); `agent_claims.sh list/todo` for the board | Codex side not inventoried; no unified cross-engine view |
| **Detect stale** | `agent_claims.sh check` (1h idle / API-error liveness); `usage_limit/detect.py` | Not unified into one "stale across both engines" report |
| **Migrate engine→engine** | `codex-import` (Codex→Claude); Codex's built-in Claude→Codex import; `session_fork` | No single "move work" command wrapping both directions |

So this is really an **epic** spanning four capabilities. Before I create it on the **Remote Control (#2)** board, two decisions:
